summary: WebFetch worked this run, so verification leans on direct first-party reads, not search snippets. Of the 45-slug batch, 39 were fetched from their own official page (checked_active), all consistent with active/general; dbos-cloud, tembo, openfaas marked low-confidence there (weak freshness signals). Six slugs omitted as unverifiable: leaseweb/infomaniak-cloud rendered near-empty content; oracle-cloud/genesis-cloud returned HTTP 403/503; google-app-engine's fetch was truncated. Two status_alerts, both from first-party pages read directly: crunchy-bridge/Crunchy Data (Snowflake's press release plus Crunchy Data's site now linking its privacy policy to Snowflake's; medium, no closing date found) and ona (ona.com states 'Part of OpenAI', dated June 11 2026 post; high). Neither applied automatically; both need review. Two redirects noted, not identity changes: linode.com/products/kubernetes now redirects to akamai.com/products/kubernetes (matches existing akamai-cloud parent), gitlab.com redirects to about.gitlab.com. Discovery searches (AI sandboxes, GPU/inference, serverless containers, shutdowns) mostly surfaced early-stage/already-cataloged entrants; one new candidate, GMI Cloud (GPU/inference provider), verified on its own site, proposed at low confidence. No other discovery hit had both a confirmed official URL read directly and a clear, non-duplicate identity.

new_candidates.name: GMI Cloud
new_candidates.summary: A GPU cloud and inference provider offering dedicated bare-metal NVIDIA GPU clusters alongside a serverless, pay-as-you-go model-serving API.
new_candidates.best_for: Teams needing both dedicated GPU capacity and scale-to-zero inference APIs without switching providers.
new_candidates.change_note: New candidate discovered via discovery search for GPU/AI cloud launches; verified directly on the official site, which describes bare-metal H100/H200 GPU clusters and a serverless inference API. Launch year and company background not stated on the page, so left unset; confidence kept low pending further verification.

status_alerts.rationale: Snowflake announced its intent to acquire Crunchy Data (maker of Crunchy Bridge) on June 2, 2025, per Snowflake's own press release. Crunchy Data's own current site (crunchydata.com) now links its footer 'Privacy Notice' to Snowflake's privacy policy page, a first-party signal consistent with the acquisition having taken effect, though no dated first-party announcement of deal closing or any Crunchy Bridge rebrand/shutdown was found. Service itself still presents as active and orderable. Flagging the ownership change for manual review rather than altering status/identity automatically.

Ona's own site (ona.com) currently carries the header 'Part of OpenAI' and a blog post dated June 11, 2026 titled 'Ona is joining OpenAI'. The product continues to operate under the Ona name and the sign-in flow still points at gitpod.io (Ona's known predecessor brand, already reflected in the catalog summary). This is a first-party-confirmed acquisition by OpenAI; flagging for review rather than changing identity/parent fields automatically, since entity/ownership changes require manual review.
